assumptions.condition: For every \(n\) and structural tuple \(\theta_n\), the observations \(Z_{1,n},\ldots,Z_{n,n}\) are independent with common law \(P_{\theta,n}\).

standard.name: Bivariate positive-coefficient linear structural causal model
Independent innovations in a linear structural causal model

novel.justification: A stable positive propagation coefficient is a proposal-specific local domain that includes fixed coefficients and slowly drifting physical transmission strengths; no compact coefficient restriction is attributed to prior work.

assumptions.condition: The distribution functions \(F_{1,n}\) and \(F_{2,n}\) are continuous.

standard.name: Continuous margins for empirical copula inference

assumptions.condition: For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), either \(A_{j,n}\equiv0\) and \(U_{j,n}(sx)/U_{j,n}(s)=x^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}\), or, uniformly for \(x\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\), \[\frac{U_{j,n}(sx)/U_{j,n}(s)-x^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}}{A_{j,n}(s)}\to x^{1/\alpha_0}\frac{x^{\rho_j}-1}{\rho_j}\] as \(s\to\infty\), uniformly over the triangular array.

novel.justification: This triangular-array uniformization is satisfied by Pareto, Burr, and Student families with tail and second-order parameters in fixed compact subsets while allowing their two tail indices to collide.

The displayed equivalence fixes the triangular-array normalization on the actual threshold range. It is compatible with the second-order quantile condition and holds exactly for Pareto tails and asymptotically for standard Hall-class tails.

assumptions.condition: The threshold-normalized tail constants satisfy \(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n}\to c_0\in(0,\infty)\).

novel.justification: This proposal-specific balance condition isolates collisions in which neither innovation vanishes merely by scale. Gnecco et al. (2021) supply only fixed-common-index comparable-tail precedent, not this unequal-index triangular-array condition.
Climate and financial pairs in the anchor contain close estimated tail exponents; a two-sided local triangular array represents empirically unresolved orderings without fixing their sign.

assumptions.condition: The sequence \((b_{1,n},b_{2,n})\) is bounded in \(\mathbb R^2\).

standard.name: Second-order bias on the root-\(k_n\) boundary
Declared worst-case second-order bias envelope for uniform tail inference

definitions.name: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\)
definitions.construction: \(\{(\theta_n)_{n\geq1}:\theta_n=(o_n,\beta_n,Q_{1,n},Q_{2,n},P_{\theta,n},\alpha_{1,n},\alpha_{2,n},c_{1,n},c_{2,n},\rho_1,\rho_2,A_{1,n},A_{2,n},U_{1,n},U_{2,n})\text{ for every }n\geq1,\text{ and the tuple sequence satisfies }\text{ass:iid-triangular-sampling},\text{ass:linear-scm},\text{ass:innovation-independence},\text{ass:coefficient-limit},\text{ass:continuous-margins},\text{ass:uniform-second-order-variation},\text{ass:uniform-tail-normalization},\text{ass:tail-constant-balance},\text{ass:local-tail-collision},\text{ass:intermediate-sequence},\text{ass:bounded-bias-coordinates},\text{ass:declared-bias-envelope}\}\)

definitions.name: empirical CTC contrast
definitions.construction: For \(a\neq b\), average the empirical rank of coordinate \(b\) over the largest \(k_n\) observations of coordinate \(a\), producing \(\widehat\Gamma_{ab,n}\), and set \(\widehat D_n=\widehat\Gamma_{12,n}-\widehat\Gamma_{21,n}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal L_\kappa\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal L_0=\{(\lambda,0,b_1,b_2):\lambda,b_1,b_2\in\mathbb R\},\qquad \mathcal L_\kappa=\{(\lambda,\kappa\lambda,b_1,b_2):\lambda,b_1,b_2\in\mathbb R\}\quad(0<\kappa<\infty),\qquad \mathcal L_\infty=\{(0,h,b_1,b_2):h,b_1,b_2\in\mathbb R\}.\] A uniform claim at regime \(\kappa\) ranges over an explicitly named compact set \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\).

definitions.name: \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\)
definitions.construction: \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)=\{\theta_n: (\theta_m)_{m\geq1}\in\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B),\ \kappa_m\to\kappa,\ (\lambda_n,h_n,b_{1,n},b_{2,n})\in K\}\) for a named compact \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{tail}}(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))\)
definitions.construction: The experiment \(\{(\mathcal T_n,P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}|_{\mathcal T_n}):\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\}\), where \(\mathcal T_n\) contains \(N_n^{(1)}\), \(N_n^{(2)}\), and both marginal upper-order-statistic arrays.

definitions.name: \(\theta_n^{\mathrm{Par}}\)
definitions.construction: Set \(o_n=\mathsf{forward}\), take independent scaled-Pareto innovations satisfying \(Q_{j,n}\{\epsilon>x\}=c_{j,n}x^{-\alpha_{j,n}}\) for \(x\geq c_{j,n}^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}\), and induce \(P_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{Par}}\) by \(X_{1,n}=\epsilon_{1,n}\) and \(X_{2,n}=\beta_nX_{1,n}+\epsilon_{2,n}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))=\left\{(C_n)_{n\geq1}: C_n\in\{\{\mathsf{forward}\},\{\mathsf{reverse}\},\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\},\ C_n\text{ is }\mathcal T_n\text{-measurable},\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{o(\theta_n)\in C_n\}\geq1-\eta\right\}.\]

definitions.name: tail-rank ambiguity criterion
definitions.construction: For compact \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\), compare the identical pair \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))}\sup_{\theta_n\in K_n(K,\kappa;B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\quad\text{and}\quad\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\theta_n\in K_n(K,\kappa;B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n^*=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\},\] using only \(\mathcal T_n\)-measurable procedures and the loss \(\mathbf 1\{C_n=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\).

definitions.name: normalized marked-intensity tangent handle
definitions.construction:
For \(b\neq a\), start from \[
u_{n,\theta}^{(a)}(B)=nP_{\theta,n}\{(X_{a,n}/q_{a,n},F_{b,n}(X_{b,n}))\in B,\ X_{a,n}>q_{a,n}\}=k_nM_{n,\theta}^{(a)}(B).\] On the forward exact-Pareto zero-bias \(X_2\) channel, split \(M_{n,\theta}^{(2)}\) into propagated and idiosyncratic components with limiting total-mass ratio \(R(\lambda)=\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0\exp(-\lambda/\alpha_0)\), and derive both conditional rank-mark kernels. Obtain the \(X_1\) channel and reverse orientation by the structural pushforwards and label exchange. Around a named \(\vartheta_0\) on each feasible face, seek dominated intensity tangents with \(\dot\ell_{a,r}=d\dot M_{\vartheta_0,r}^{(a)}/dM_{\vartheta_0}^{(a)}\), then target \[\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathrm{cen}}_n(r)=k_n^{-1/2}\sum_{a=1}^2\int\dot\ell_{a,r}(z)\{dN_n^{(a)}(z)-k_n\,dM_{\vartheta_0}^{(a)}(z)\},\qquad I_{rs}=\sum_{a=1}^2\int\dot\ell_{a,r}(z)\dot\ell_{a,s}(z)\,dM_{\vartheta_0}^{(a)}(z).\]

definitions.name: finite-grid envelope-conditional direction handle
definitions.construction: On the reported finite grid \(\mathcal G_n\), condition on the declared envelope \(B_n\), use simultaneous multiplier bands at level \(1-\eta\), subtract \(B_n(k)\), retain thresholds whose CTC and tail-index scores are mutually stable, and return exactly one of the two singletons or \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\). Repeat the construction for \(B_n^{(c)}=cB_n\), \(c\in\mathcal C\), with the calibration constrained so that \(c\leq c'\) implies \(C_n^{*,(c)}\subseteq C_n^{*,(c')}\).

definitions.name: opposite-report tail-rank contiguity handle
definitions.construction: Use a Le Cam two-point or Assouad family that changes the structural orientation and the sign of the local tail gap while perturbing inverse tail weights and second-order auxiliaries so that the \(\mathcal T_n\)-likelihood ratios have bounded pairwise divergence.

statements.statement:
For the forward scaled exact-Pareto tuple \(\theta_n^{\mathrm{Par}}\), let \(u_n\to\infty\) satisfy
\[
\frac{u_n}{\beta_n c_{1,n}^{1/\alpha_{1,n}}+c_{2,n}^{1/\alpha_{2,n}}}\to\infty,
\qquad |\Delta_n|\log u_n\leq L,
\]
and let \(r_n(u)=\beta_n^{\alpha_{1,n}}(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n})u^{-\Delta_n}\). For every such sequence,
\[
E_{P_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{Par}}}[F_{1,n}(X_{1,n})\mid X_{2,n}>u_n]
=\frac12+\frac12\frac{r_n(u_n)}{1+r_n(u_n)}+o(1).
\]
If, in addition, \(\Delta_n\log c_{2,n}\to0\), then \(\Gamma_{12,n}(t_n)=1+o(1)\); and if \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in\mathbb R\), then
\[
D_n(t_n)\to g_{\alpha_0,\beta_0,c_0}(\lambda)
=\{2[1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0e^{-\lambda/\alpha_0}]\}^{-1}.
\]
The limiting curve tends to \(1/2\) as \(\lambda\to+\infty\), equals \(\{2(1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0)\}^{-1}\) at \(\lambda=0\), and tends to zero as \(\lambda\to-\infty\).
statements.justification: This early kill test establishes a nonconstant local population object before the joint experiment is attempted.
statements.gap: Leimenstoll and Schienle (2026, Proposition 3.1; proof in Appendix A.1) give only fixed heterogeneous-tail endpoints, while Gnecco et al. (2021, Lemma 1) give the fixed-common-index endpoint; neither states the local transition curve.
statements.consumer: The curve calibrates finite-threshold CTC contrasts in the anchor's climate and finance analyses when estimated innovation indices are close.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
s_{j,n}=c_{j,n}^{1/\alpha_{j,n}},\qquad
A_n=\beta_n\epsilon_{1,n},\qquad B_n'=\epsilon_{2,n}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}pareto\text{-}witness}\), \(s_{j,n}\) is the lower endpoint of the scaled-Pareto law \(Q_{j,n}\).  For any \(u\) above both component supports define
\[
p_{1,n}(u)=P(A_n>u)
=c_{1,n}\beta_n^{\alpha_{1,n}}u^{-\alpha_{1,n}},
\qquad
p_{2,n}(u)=P(B_n'>u)=c_{2,n}u^{-\alpha_{2,n}}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}tail\text{-}collision}\) implies that, for some constants \(0<a_-<a_+<\infty\),
\[
a_-\leq\alpha_{j,n}\leq a_+,
\qquad j\in\{1,2\},
\tag{2}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}coefficient\text{-}limit}\) similarly bounds \(\beta_n\) above and away from zero.  Hence the support condition on \(u_n\) gives
\[
\frac{u_n}{\beta_ns_{1,n}}\to\infty,
\qquad
\frac{u_n}{s_{2,n}}\to\infty,
\qquad
p_{1,n}(u_n)\vee p_{2,n}(u_n)\to0.
\tag{3}
\]

We first establish a ratio-free convolution-tail estimate.  Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  Once \(\delta u_n\) exceeds both component supports, independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}innovation\text{-}independence}\) and the inclusions
\[
\{A_n>u_n\}\cup\{B_n'>u_n\}
\subseteq\{A_n+B_n'>u_n\}
\]
and
\[
\{A_n+B_n'>u_n\}
\subseteq
\{A_n>(1-\delta)u_n\}\cup
\{B_n'>(1-\delta)u_n\}\cup
\bigl(\{A_n>\delta u_n\}\cap\{B_n'>\delta u_n\}\bigr)
\]
give
\[
\begin{split}
p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}-p_{1,n}p_{2,n}
&\leq P(A_n+B_n'>u_n)\\
&\leq p_{1,n}(1-\delta)^{-\alpha_{1,n}}
 +p_{2,n}(1-\delta)^{-\alpha_{2,n}}
 +p_{1,n}p_{2,n}\delta^{-\alpha_{1,n}-\alpha_{2,n}},
\end{split}
\tag{4}
\]
where \(p_{j,n}=p_{j,n}(u_n)\).  Crucially, no bound on \(p_{1,n}/p_{2,n}\) is needed, because
\[
0\leq\frac{p_{1,n}p_{2,n}}{p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}}
\leq\min(p_{1,n},p_{2,n})\to0
\tag{5}
\]
by (3).  Divide (4) by \(p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}\), use (2) and (5), first let \(n\to\infty\), and then let \(\delta\downarrow0\).  The lower and upper bounds both tend to one, so
\[
P(A_n+B_n'>u_n)
=p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}+o(p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}).
\tag{6}
\]
This argument applies to every level sequence satisfying the two support-ratio limits in (3), regardless of the ratio of its two component tails.

Let \(H_n=F_{1,n}(\epsilon_{1,n})\).  The scaled-Pareto distribution is continuous, so the probability integral transform gives \(E(H_n)=1/2\).  On \(\{A_n>u_n\}\), the exact Pareto formula yields
\[
0\leq1-H_n=c_{1,n}\epsilon_{1,n}^{-\alpha_{1,n}}
\leq c_{1,n}(u_n/\beta_n)^{-\alpha_{1,n}}=p_{1,n}.
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently,
\[
E\!\left[H_n\mathbf1\{A_n>u_n\}\right]
=p_{1,n}+O(p_{1,n}^2).
\tag{8}
\]
Independence gives
\[
E\!\left[H_n\mathbf1\{B_n'>u_n\}\right]=\frac12p_{2,n},
\qquad
0\leq E\!\left[H_n\mathbf1\{A_n>u_n,B_n'>u_n\}\right]
\leq p_{1,n}p_{2,n}.
\tag{9}
\]
By (6), the probability of
\(\{A_n+B_n'>u_n\}\setminus(\{A_n>u_n\}\cup\{B_n'>u_n\})\)
is \(o(p_{1,n}+p_{2,n})\).  Since \(0\leq H_n\leq1\), equations (5), (8), and (9) therefore imply
\[
E\!\left[H_n\mathbf1\{A_n+B_n'>u_n\}\right]
=p_{1,n}+\frac12p_{2,n}+o(p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}).
\tag{10}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}linear\text{-}scm}\) and the forward orientation in \(\mathrm{def{:}pareto\text{-}witness}\), \(X_{1,n}=\epsilon_{1,n}\) and \(X_{2,n}=A_n+B_n'\).  Dividing (10) by (6), and using
\[
\frac{p_{1,n}(u)}{p_{2,n}(u)}
=\beta_n^{\alpha_{1,n}}\frac{c_{1,n}}{c_{2,n}}u^{-\Delta_n}
=r_n(u),
\tag{11}
\]
proves, for every level sequence in the proposed claim,
\[
E[F_{1,n}(X_{1,n})\mid X_{2,n}>u_n]
=\frac12+\frac12\frac{r_n(u_n)}{1+r_n(u_n)}+o(1).
\tag{12}
\]
The localization bound \(|\Delta_n|\log u_n\leq L\), together with \(\mathrm{ass{:}coefficient\text{-}limit}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}tail\text{-}constant\text{-}balance}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}tail\text{-}collision}\), also bounds \(r_n(u_n)\) above and away from zero, although the ratio-free proof of (6) did not require that fact.

We next pass to the quantile threshold in \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\text{-}threshold\text{-}ctc}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}intermediate\text{-}sequence}\) gives \(t_n=n/k_n\to\infty\).  Define the exact \((1-1/t_n)\)-quantile of \(X_{1,n}\) by
\[
q_{1,n}=s_{1,n}t_n^{1/\alpha_{1,n}}.
\tag{13}
\]
Assume now the stated scale-locality condition \(\Delta_n\log c_{2,n}\to0\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}tail\text{-}constant\text{-}balance}\) gives \(\log(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n})=O(1)\), and direct algebra gives
\[
\log\frac{q_{1,n}}{s_{2,n}}
=\frac{\log t_n}{\alpha_{1,n}}
 +\frac{\log(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n})}{\alpha_{1,n}}
 -\frac{\Delta_n\log c_{2,n}}{\alpha_{1,n}\alpha_{2,n}}
\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{14}
\]
Together with \(q_{1,n}/s_{1,n}=t_n^{1/\alpha_{1,n}}\to\infty\) and the positive coefficient limit, (14) implies
\[
\frac{\beta_nq_{1,n}}{\beta_ns_{1,n}+s_{2,n}}\to\infty.
\tag{15}
\]
At the level \(v_n=\beta_nq_{1,n}\), the two component-tail probabilities in (1) satisfy
\[
p_{1,n}(v_n)=\frac1{t_n}\to0,
\qquad
p_{2,n}(v_n)=\left(\frac{s_{2,n}}{v_n}\right)^{\alpha_{2,n}}\to0.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus the ratio-free estimate (6), now applied at \(v_n\) using (15)--(16), gives
\[
P(X_{2,n}>\beta_nq_{1,n})
=\{p_{1,n}(v_n)+p_{2,n}(v_n)\}\{1+o(1)\}\to0.
\tag{17}
\]
On the conditioning event \(F_{1,n}(X_{1,n})>1-1/t_n\), continuity of the first Pareto law gives \(X_{1,n}>q_{1,n}\), hence \(X_{2,n}\geq\beta_nX_{1,n}>\beta_nq_{1,n}\).  Monotonicity of \(F_{2,n}\), (17), and the definition of \(\Gamma_{12,n}\) yield the audited bound
\[
0\leq1-\Gamma_{12,n}(t_n)
\leq1-F_{2,n}(\beta_nq_{1,n})
=P(X_{2,n}>\beta_nq_{1,n})\to0.
\tag{18}
\]
This proves \(\Gamma_{12,n}(t_n)=1+o(1)\) without imposing any boundedness condition on \(\Delta_n\log t_n\).

Finally suppose \(\lambda_n=\Delta_n\log t_n\to\lambda\in\mathbb R\), and let \(q_{2,n}\) be the exact \((1-1/t_n)\)-quantile of \(X_{2,n}\).  Each scaled-Pareto component has a strictly positive continuous density on the interior of its support; independence therefore makes the convolution distribution continuous and strictly increasing above \(\beta_ns_{1,n}+s_{2,n}\), so this exact quantile exists and is unique.  Set
\[
a_n=\beta_ns_{1,n}t_n^{1/\alpha_{1,n}},
\qquad b_n=s_{2,n}t_n^{1/\alpha_{2,n}}.
\tag{19}
\]
Since \(X_{2,n}\geq A_n\vee B_n'\), while
\(P(A_n>\beta_ns_{1,n}(2t_n)^{1/\alpha_{1,n}})=P(B_n'>s_{2,n}(2t_n)^{1/\alpha_{2,n}})=1/(2t_n)\), the union bound gives the explicit quantile sandwich
\[
\max(a_n,b_n)\leq q_{2,n}
\leq\beta_ns_{1,n}(2t_n)^{1/\alpha_{1,n}}
 +s_{2,n}(2t_n)^{1/\alpha_{2,n}}.
\tag{20}
\]
By (2), the right side is at most \(C(a_n+b_n)\leq2C\max(a_n,b_n)\) for a fixed finite \(C\).  Therefore
\[
0\leq\log q_{2,n}-\max(\log a_n,\log b_n)\leq\log(2C).
\tag{21}
\]
The lower bound in (20) also gives
\[
\frac{q_{2,n}}{\beta_ns_{1,n}+s_{2,n}}
\geq\frac12\min\!\left(t_n^{1/\alpha_{1,n}},t_n^{1/\alpha_{2,n}}\right)
\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{22}
\]

Scale locality and tail-constant balance imply
\[
\Delta_n\log c_{1,n}
=\Delta_n\log c_{2,n}+\Delta_n\log(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n})\to0.
\tag{23}
\]
Using (19), \(\beta_n\to\beta_0>0\), the two index limits, (23), and \(\Delta_n\log t_n\to\lambda\), we obtain
\[
\begin{split}
\Delta_n\log a_n
&=\Delta_n\log\beta_n
 +\frac{\Delta_n}{\alpha_{1,n}}(\log c_{1,n}+\log t_n)
\longrightarrow\frac{\lambda}{\alpha_0},\\
\Delta_n\log b_n
&=\frac{\Delta_n}{\alpha_{2,n}}(\log c_{2,n}+\log t_n)
\longrightarrow\frac{\lambda}{\alpha_0}.
\end{split}
\tag{24}
\]
Because \(\Delta_n\to0\), (21) and (24) prove directly, with no circular appeal to a tail equation, that
\[
\Delta_n\log q_{2,n}\longrightarrow\frac{\lambda}{\alpha_0}.
\tag{25}
\]
Equations (22) and (2) show that both component tails at \(q_{2,n}\) vanish, so the ratio-free derivation of (12) applies at \(u_n=q_{2,n}\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{ass{:}coefficient\text{-}limit}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}tail\text{-}constant\text{-}balance}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}tail\text{-}collision}\), and (25) give
\[
r_n(q_{2,n})
=\beta_n^{\alpha_{1,n}}\frac{c_{1,n}}{c_{2,n}}
  \exp\{-\Delta_n\log q_{2,n}\}
\longrightarrow R(\lambda)
:=\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0e^{-\lambda/\alpha_0}.
\tag{26}
\]
Continuity makes \(F_{2,n}(X_{2,n})>1-1/t_n\) equivalent to \(X_{2,n}>q_{2,n}\).  Hence (12) and (26) yield
\[
\Gamma_{21,n}(t_n)
=\frac12+\frac12\frac{R(\lambda)}{1+R(\lambda)}+o(1).
\tag{27}
\]
Subtracting (27) from (18), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\text{-}threshold\text{-}ctc}\), proves
\[
D_n(t_n)\longrightarrow
\frac1{2\{1+R(\lambda)\}}
=\{2[1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0e^{-\lambda/\alpha_0}]\}^{-1}
=g_{\alpha_0,\beta_0,c_0}(\lambda).
\tag{28}
\]
At \(\lambda=0\), (28) is \(\{2(1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0)\}^{-1}\).  Since \(R(\lambda)\to0\) as \(\lambda\to+\infty\) and \(R(\lambda)\to\infty\) as \(\lambda\to-\infty\), (28) tends respectively to \(1/2\) and to zero, completing the proof.

statements.statement: If its parameter sequences obey \(\beta_n\to\beta_0>0\), \(\alpha_{j,n}\to\alpha_0\), and \(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n}\to c_0\in(0,\infty)\), then the structural tuple sequence \((\theta_n^{\mathrm{Par}})_{n\geq1}\) belongs to \(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\), with \(A_{1,n}=A_{2,n}=0\), for every intermediate sequence \(k_n\) and every declared nonnegative envelope \(B_n\).
statements.justification: The transition curve is load-bearing only if its structural witness is inside the tuple class.
statements.gap: The anchor uses Pareto innovations in simulations but does not formulate local triangular-array structural membership.
statements.consumer: Membership makes the curve an auditable calibration submodel for the marked experiment.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix any parameter sequence satisfying the hypotheses of the proposition, any intermediate sequence \(k_n\), and any declared envelope \(B_n:\mathcal G_n\to[0,\infty)\).  We verify, one by one, the conditions in the definition of \(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\).

First consider the scaled-Pareto law in \(\theta_n^{\mathrm{Par}}\).  Its lower endpoint is \(a_{j,n}=c_{j,n}^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}>0\), and its distribution function is
\[
 F_{\epsilon_j,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&0\leq x<a_{j,n},\\
 1-c_{j,n}x^{-\alpha_{j,n}},&x\geq a_{j,n}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two branches agree at \(a_{j,n}\), because \(c_{j,n}a_{j,n}^{-\alpha_{j,n}}=1\); hence each innovation law is continuous and atomless.  Solving
\(1-c_{j,n}x^{-\alpha_{j,n}}=1-1/s\) gives, for every \(s>1\),
\[
 U_{j,n}(s)=(c_{j,n}s)^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}. \tag{1}
\]
In particular, because \(t_n=n/k_n>1\),
\[
 \frac{U_{j,n}(t_n)^{\alpha_{j,n}}}{t_n}
 =\frac{c_{j,n}t_n}{t_n}=c_{j,n}. \tag{2}
\]
Thus the scale constants used to construct the Pareto laws equal the threshold-normalized constants required in the structural tuple; there is no normalization mismatch.

By the construction in \(\mathrm{def:pareto\text{-}witness}\), \(o_n=\mathsf{forward}\), the innovations are independent, and
\[
 X_{1,n}=\epsilon_{1,n},\qquad
 X_{2,n}=\beta_nX_{1,n}+\epsilon_{2,n}. \tag{3}
\]
Equation (3) is precisely the forward clause of \(\mathrm{ass:linear\text{-}scm}\), while independence is \(\mathrm{ass:innovation\text{-}independence}\).  The assumed limit \(\beta_n\to\beta_0>0\) verifies \(\mathrm{ass:coefficient\text{-}limit}\).  The first margin is continuous by the preceding display.  For every \(x\geq0\), innovation independence and atomlessness give
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\beta_n\epsilon_{1,n}+\epsilon_{2,n}=x\right)
 =E\!\left[\Pr\!\left(\epsilon_{2,n}=x-\beta_n\epsilon_{1,n}\mid\epsilon_{1,n}\right)\right]=0. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently the second margin has no atoms and its distribution function is continuous.  This proves \(\mathrm{ass:continuous\text{-}margins}\).  Taking \(Z_{1,n},\ldots,Z_{n,n}\) under the product law \(\bigl(P_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{Par}}\bigr)^{\otimes n}\) verifies the independent common-law requirement in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}triangular\text{-}sampling}\).

Set \(A_{1,n}=A_{2,n}=0\).  From (1), whenever \(s>1\) and \(sx>1\),
\[
 \frac{U_{j,n}(sx)}{U_{j,n}(s)}=x^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}. \tag{5}
\]
For every compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), the restriction \(sx>1\) holds for all sufficiently large \(s\), uniformly in \(x\) in that compact subset.  Therefore the zero-auxiliary branch of \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}second\text{-}order\text{-}variation}\) holds exactly, so its remainder is identically zero and hence uniform over the triangular array.

Next fix \(m>1\).  The hypotheses \(\alpha_{j,n}\to\alpha_0>0\) imply that, eventually, \(0<\alpha_{j,n}\leq2\alpha_0\).  The intermediate-sequence condition gives \(t_n=n/k_n\to\infty\), and hence
\[
 \inf_{s\in[m^{-1},m]}
 \frac{U_{j,n}(t_n)s}{a_{j,n}}
 =m^{-1}t_n^{1/\alpha_{j,n}}
 \geq m^{-1}t_n^{1/(2\alpha_0)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{6}
\]
Thus the Pareto survival formula applies throughout the indicated range for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Using (2), for those \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{s\in[m^{-1},m]}
 \left|
 \frac{Q_{j,n}\{\epsilon>U_{j,n}(t_n)s\}}
 {c_{j,n}\{U_{j,n}(t_n)s\}^{-\alpha_{j,n}}}-1
 \right|=0. \tag{7}
\]
This proves \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}tail\text{-}normalization}\).  The assumed convergence \(c_{1,n}/c_{2,n}\to c_0\in(0,\infty)\) is exactly \(\mathrm{ass:tail\text{-}constant\text{-}balance}\).

The two assumed limits \(\alpha_{1,n}\to\alpha_0\) and \(\alpha_{2,n}\to\alpha_0\) yield
\[
 \Delta_n=\alpha_{1,n}-\alpha_{2,n}\longrightarrow0, \tag{8}
\]
so \(\mathrm{ass:local\text{-}tail\text{-}collision}\) holds.  The chosen \(k_n\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:intermediate\text{-}sequence}\) by hypothesis.  Finally, the zero auxiliaries imply
\[
 b_{j,n}=\sqrt{k_n}A_{j,n}(t_n)=0,\qquad
 \sqrt{k}\,|A_{j,n}(n/k)|=0\leq B_n(k)
 \quad(k\in\mathcal G_n). \tag{9}
\]
The first equality in (9) verifies \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}bias\text{-}coordinates}\), and the inequality verifies \(\mathrm{ass:declared\text{-}bias\text{-}envelope}\); nonnegativity of \(B_n\) is used in the last step.

Equations (2)--(9), together with the structural construction (3), verify every member property listed in \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}model\text{-}class}\).  Hence \((\theta_n^{\mathrm{Par}})_{n\geq1}\in\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\), with \(A_{1,n}=A_{2,n}=0\), for every admissible \(k_n\) and every declared nonnegative \(B_n\), as claimed.

statements.statement: Exactly \(h_n=\kappa_n\lambda_n\). If \(\kappa_n\to0\), every finite local limit lies in \(\mathcal L_0\), so finite \(\lambda\) requires \(h=0\). If \(\kappa_n\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), every finite local limit lies in \(\mathcal L_\kappa\), so \(h=\kappa\lambda\). If \(\kappa_n\to\infty\), the finite-dimensional local face is \(\mathcal L_\infty\), so finite \(h\) requires \(\lambda=0\); any nonzero finite limit of \(\lambda_n\) instead satisfies \( |h_n|\to\infty\) and is a separated boundary. For \(k_n=n^\nu\), \(0<\nu<1\), this last regime contains the nonempty band \(k_n^{-1/2}\ll|\Delta_n|\ll1/\log t_n\).
statements.justification: The result prevents impossible uniformity over independent logarithmic and root-threshold coordinates.
statements.gap: Beirlant, Bouquiaux, and Werker (2006, Theorems 2.1--2.2) supply the root-\(k_n\) coordinate, while Leimenstoll and Schienle (2026, Proposition 3.1) use fixed tail ordering; neither states this compatibility geometry.
statements.consumer: Every limit experiment and ambiguity calculation can now be indexed by a genuine feasible compactum.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def{:}collision\text{-}coordinates}\),
\[
 h_n=\sqrt{k_n}\Delta_n
 =\frac{\sqrt{k_n}}{\log t_n}\,\Delta_n\log t_n
 =\kappa_n\lambda_n. \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}intermediate\text{-}sequence}\) implies \(t_n=n/k_n\to\infty\), so \(\log t_n>0\) eventually and every division in (1) is valid.

If \(\kappa_n\to0\) and \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in\mathbb R\), (1) gives \(h_n\to0\); hence every finite limit has the form \((\lambda,0,b_1,b_2)\in\mathcal L_0\).  If \(\kappa_n\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), (1) gives \(h=\kappa\lambda\), exactly the constraint defining \(\mathcal L_\kappa\).  If \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) and \(h_n\to h\in\mathbb R\), then \(\lambda_n=h_n/\kappa_n\to0\), which gives \(\mathcal L_\infty\).  Conversely, if \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\neq0\) in this last regime, then (1) gives \(|h_n|=\kappa_n|\lambda_n|\to\infty\).  These are precisely the three faces in \(\mathrm{def{:}feasible\text{-}local\text{-}spaces}\).

For \(k_n=n^\nu\), \(0<\nu<1\), one has
\[
 t_n=n^{1-\nu},\qquad
 \kappa_n=\frac{n^{\nu/2}}{(1-\nu)\log n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The band is nonempty: for example,
\[
 d_n=\frac{n^{-\nu/4}}{\sqrt{\log n}}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \frac{d_n}{k_n^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{n^{\nu/4}}{\sqrt{\log n}}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 d_n\log t_n
 =(1-\nu)n^{-\nu/4}\sqrt{\log n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus \(k_n^{-1/2}\ll d_n\ll1/\log t_n\), proving the last assertion.

statements.statement: Conditionally on the declared envelope \(B_n\), use the finite-grid envelope-conditional handle to construct \((C_n^*)\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))\). For every \(\kappa\in[0,\infty]\) and named compact \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\), give an oracle ambiguity bound over \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\) in terms of the reported finite grid \(\mathcal G_n\), \(\eta\), \(B_n(k)\), \(s_{\mathrm{CTC},n}(k)\), and \(s_{\mathrm{idx},n}(k)\); require \(\sup_{\theta_n\in K_n(K,\kappa;B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n^*=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\to0\) whenever the best grid point has both separations diverging beyond its simultaneous critical value and declared bias envelope. On the reported finite grid \(\mathcal C\), also construct \(C_n^{*,(c)}\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B^{(c)}))\) for \(B_n^{(c)}=cB_n\), with \(c\leq c'\) implying \(C_n^{*,(c)}\subseteq C_n^{*,(c')}\). Establish validity at \(\Delta_n=0\) and equivariance under exchanging variable labels.
statements.justification: A three-valued direction set is the non-vacuous honest object at equality and after threshold selection.
statements.gap: Carpentier and Kim (2014) and Sasaki and Wang (2024) concern scalar tail parameters. Pasche et al. (2023) provide a parametric adjusted CTC estimator and permutation test, and Bodik et al. (2024) provide a time-series CTC estimator while leaving its distribution, bias correction, and rigorous testing open; neither gives an envelope-conditional honest set at a static local index collision.
statements.consumer: Users receive either a calibrated arrow or an explicit ambiguous report for close-tail climate and finance pairs.

statements.statement: For each \(\kappa\in[0,\infty]\) and named compact \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\), use the opposite-report tail-rank contiguity handle to determine an explicit \(v_\eta(K)\) such that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))}\sup_{\theta_n\in K_n(K,\kappa;B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\geq v_\eta(K),\] and prove for the same \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\), coverage class, loss, tail-rank measurability restriction, and limit order that \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\theta_n\in K_n(K,\kappa;B)}P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n^*=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\leq v_\eta(K).\] The converse is expressly conditional on \(\mathcal T_n\) and is not a claim about unrestricted full-distribution causal discovery.
statements.justification: Matching bounds certify when a full direction set is forced by the available tail-rank information.
statements.gap: Novak (2014) and Beirlant et al. (2006) lower-bound marginal tail inference. Pasche et al. (2023) and Bodik et al. (2024) provide CTC procedures but no minimax ambiguity loss or bounded-divergence opposite-orientation construction for this marked tail-rank experiment.
statements.consumer: An ambiguous empirical conclusion becomes a certified information limit rather than an undocumented threshold failure.

statements.statement: Under the frozen collision model, the requested finite-coordinate uniform local experiment does not exist as stated.  For every regime limit \(\kappa\) and every compact \(K\subset\mathcal L_\kappa\) containing \((0,0,0,0)\), the forward zero-bias exact-Pareto subclass contains two arrays with identical \((\lambda_n,h_n,b_{1,n},b_{2,n})=(0,0,0,0)\) whose restrictions to \(\mathcal T_n\) are asymptotically perfectly distinguishable.  In addition, even at a fixed common index, the two exceedance point measures have order-\(k_n\) overlap, so a joint information form cannot in general be obtained by summing the two marginal intensity informations \(I_{rs}=\sum_{a=1}^2\int\dot\ell_{a,r}\dot\ell_{a,s}\,dM_{\vartheta_0}^{(a)}\).  A valid formulation must at least add a root-\(k_n\) common-tail-index coordinate and a joint overlap intensity, or an equivalent paired marked point process, before bias drifts and a uniform likelihood remainder can be defined.
statements.proof_tex:
We give two explicit certificates, both inside the exact-Pareto zero-bias subclass.  Fix the forward orientation, \(\beta_n=\beta_0\), \(c_{1,n}=c_0\), \(c_{2,n}=1\), and \(A_{1,n}=A_{2,n}=0\).  For the first array set
\(\alpha_{1,n}=\alpha_{2,n}=\alpha_0\); for the second set
\[
 \alpha_{1,n}=\alpha_{2,n}=\alpha_0+k_n^{-1/4}.
\]
Both arrays satisfy \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}tail\text{-}collision}\), have \(\Delta_n=0\), and therefore have the same collision coordinates
\[
 (\lambda_n,h_n,b_{1,n},b_{2,n})=(0,0,0,0).
\]
All other membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}collision\text{-}model\text{-}class}\) hold: the innovations are independent continuous exact-Pareto variables, the coefficient is positive and constant, the second-order auxiliaries vanish, and every declared nonnegative bias envelope contains zero.

The marginal upper-order-statistic array belongs to \(\mathcal T_n\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}tail\text{-}rank\text{-}experiment}\).  From its first coordinate define the Hill statistic
\[
 H_n=\frac1{k_n}\sum_{j=1}^{k_n}
 \log\frac{X_{(n-j+1),1,n}}{X_{(n-k_n),1,n}}.
\]
If the common Pareto index is \(a>0\), then \(\log X_{i,1,n}\) is exponential with rate \(a\).  The elementary exponential-spacing representation gives
\[
 H_n\ \stackrel{d}{=}\ \frac1{k_n}\sum_{j=1}^{k_n}E_{j,n},
 \qquad E_{1,n},\ldots,E_{k_n,n}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Exp}(a).
\]
Indeed, successive upper exponential spacings have respective rates \(a,2a,\ldots,k_na\), and multiplying the spacing with rate \(ja\) by \(j\) gives an exponential variable of rate \(a\); expanding the sum defining \(H_n\) produces exactly these multiplied spacings.  Hence
\[
 E_aH_n=\frac1a,qquad \operatorname{Var}_a(H_n)=\frac1{k_na^2}. \tag{1}
\]
For \(a_{0,n}=\alpha_0\) and \(a_{1,n}=\alpha_0+k_n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \left|\frac1{a_{1,n}}-\frac1{a_{0,n}}\right|
 =\frac{k_n^{-1/4}}{\alpha_0(\alpha_0+k_n^{-1/4})}
 \asymp k_n^{-1/4}. \tag{2}
\]
The test that compares \(H_n\) with the midpoint of the two means has, by Chebyshev's inequality and (1)--(2), the sum of its two error probabilities bounded by \(O(k_n^{-1/2})\to0\).  Thus the total-variation distance between the two restrictions to \(\mathcal T_n\) tends to one although their entire declared finite local coordinate vectors coincide.  In particular, no likelihood expansion centered only at \((\lambda,h,b_1,b_2)\) can hold uniformly over \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\): the omitted common-index coordinate
\(\sqrt{k_n}\{(\alpha_{1,n}+\alpha_{2,n})/2-\alpha_0\}\) equals zero in the first array and diverges in the second.

There is a separate obstruction to the proposed information form.  Keep the first array and write
\[
 Y_{a,n}=N_n^{(a)}((1,\infty)\times[0,1]),\qquad a\in\{1,2\}.
\]
Because the marginal quantiles are continuous, \(EY_{1,n}=EY_{2,n}=n/t_n=k_n\).  Here \(q_{1,n}=(c_0t_n)^{1/\alpha_0}\).  The same direct one-large-jump bounds used for two independent Pareto variables give
\[
 P(\beta_0\epsilon_{1,n}+\epsilon_{2,n}>x)
 =(\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0+1)x^{-\alpha_0}\{1+o(1)\},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \frac{q_{2,n}}{q_{1,n}}
 \longrightarrow\left(\frac{\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0+1}{c_0}\right)^{1/\alpha_0},
 \qquad
 \frac{q_{2,n}}{\beta_0q_{1,n}}
 \longrightarrow\left(1+\frac1{\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0}\right)^{1/\alpha_0}>1. \tag{3}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the event \(\{\epsilon_{1,n}>q_{2,n}/\beta_0\}\) is contained in both exceedance events.  Independence across observations from \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}triangular\text{-}sampling}\), followed by (3), yields
\[
\begin{split}
 \frac1{k_n}\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{1,n},Y_{2,n})
 &=\frac n{k_n}\left[P(X_{1,n}>q_{1,n},X_{2,n}>q_{2,n})-t_n^{-2}\right]\\
 &\geq t_nP(\epsilon_{1,n}>q_{2,n}/\beta_0)-t_n^{-1}
 \longrightarrow\frac{\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0}{1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0}>0.
\end{split}\tag{4}
\]
Thus the limiting compensated measures possess a nonzero cross-covariance measure.  The two marginal normalized intensities \(M_{n,\theta}^{(1)}\) and \(M_{n,\theta}^{(2)}\) do not record that measure, while the displayed candidate \(I_{rs}\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}experiment\text{-}handle}\) contains no cross term.  Equations (1)--(4) prove both asserted obstructions and identify the minimum repairs required before a joint LAN calculation can be valid.

statements.statement:
Let \(C_n^0\) be the constant sample map
\[
 C_n^*(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=C_n^0(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}
 \qquad\text{for every }(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in(\mathbb R_+^2)^n,
\]
and, for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), let \(C_n^{*,(c)}=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\).  For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
 (C_n^*)\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)),
 \qquad
 (C_n^{*,(c)})\in\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B^{(c)}))
 \quad(c\in\mathcal C).
\]
The coverage probability is exactly one for every model member, including every member with \(\Delta_n=0\).  The construction is equivariant under exchanging the two variable labels, and
\[
 c\leq c'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 C_n^{*,(c)}=C_n^{*,(c')}=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}},
\]
so the sensitivity family is nested.  Moreover,
\[
 P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n^*=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}=1
\]
for every \(\theta_n\); hence its worst-case ambiguity probability over every nonempty \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\) is exactly one.  This is the strongest direction-set conclusion established from the frozen calibration handle: the declared envelope controls \(\sqrt{k}\lvert A_{j,n}(n/k)\rvert\), not the bias of \(\widehat D_n\), while the proposed four-coordinate summed-marginal experiment omits a common-index coordinate and the order-\(k_n\) overlap of the two exceedance channels.  No vanishing-ambiguity conclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: The frozen premises certify an exact, uniformly honest fallback set, while the joint-experiment obstruction prevents the advertised nontrivial calibration from being claimed.
statements.gap: Scalar tail-index confidence results and one-process tail-copula multipliers do not validate a paired marked CTC band with overlap covariance and CTC bias control.
statements.consumer: Climate and finance analyses can report the full direction alphabet as an exactly covered ambiguity set; no calibrated arrow is claimed at the collision boundary.

statements.proof_tex:
The class \(\mathcal H_\eta(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B))\) is nonempty by \(\mathrm{thm{:}constant\text{-}honest\text{-}direction\text{-}set}\).  For every member \((C_n)\) of this class, every \(\theta_n\), and every \(n\), probability axioms give
\[
 0\leq P_{\theta,n}^{\otimes n}\{C_n=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\leq1. \tag{3}
\]
Because \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\) is nonempty eventually, taking the supremum over this set preserves both bounds in (3).  Taking the infimum over the nonempty honesty class again preserves the bounds, and taking the limit inferior proves (1).

For the particular constant construction, the event in (3) is the whole sample space.  Its probability is therefore one for every \(\theta_n\).  The eventual nonemptiness of \(K_n(K,\kappa;B)\) implies that the supremum in (2) is one for every sufficiently large \(n\), and hence its limit superior is one.

Now suppose that \((0,0,0,0)\in K\).  The first certificate in \(\mathrm{thm{:}joint\text{-}collision\text{-}experiment\text{-}obstruction}\) supplies two forward, zero-bias, exact-Pareto arrays with identical values
\[
 (\lambda_n,h_n,b_{1,n},b_{2,n})=(0,0,0,0)
\]
whose restrictions to \(\mathcal T_n\) have total-variation distance tending to one.  Thus those four coordinates do not index a unique local tail-rank experiment.  The second certificate in that theorem gives a strictly positive limiting order-\(k_n\) covariance between the two exceedance counts, whereas the candidate information form in \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}experiment\text{-}handle}\) is only the sum of the two marginal intensity informations.  Hence the proposed summed-marginal experiment supplies neither the unique experiment law nor the joint information required to calculate a Le Cam ambiguity value.  The opposite-report handle in \(\mathrm{def{:}ambiguity\text{-}lower\text{-}bound\text{-}handle}\) names a desired construction but proves no bounded divergence for an opposite-orientation collision pair.  Therefore no positive collision-specific lower bound follows from that handle, while (2) is the only achieved upper value.  This establishes exactly the asserted bracket and obstruction, without making a claim about an augmented paired experiment or unrestricted full-distribution causal discovery.
statements.justification: This records the exact ambiguity bounds that survive the malformed four-coordinate experiment and isolates why a collision-specific matching value is not yet defined.
statements.gap: Existing marginal tail lower bounds provide neither a bounded-divergence opposite-orientation collision pair nor the missing joint overlap likelihood for this tail-rank experiment.
statements.consumer: An ambiguity probability of one is identified as the achieved honest fallback, not misreported as a sharp information limit.

sampling_model.design: Triangular-array independent sampling from structural tuples in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\); inference is conditional on the declared bias envelope and restricted to the CTC tail-rank sigma-field \(\mathcal T_n\).
sampling_model.units: At row \(n\), \(Z_{1,n},\ldots,Z_{n,n}\) have common induced law \(P_{\theta,n}\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no assigned treatment; \(o(\theta_n)\) is a structural tuple component, not a functional asserted to be unique from the observational law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Marginal ranks and tail-index scores are evaluated on the reported finite grid \(\mathcal G_n\). The envelope \(B_n\) is declared rather than estimated, and \(B_n^{(c)}=cB_n\) is reported on the finite sensitivity grid \(\mathcal C\).

estimand_functional: \(\widehat D_n=\widehat\Gamma_{12,n}-\widehat\Gamma_{21,n}\), with \(g_{\alpha_0,\beta_0,c_0}(\lambda)=\{2[1+\beta_0^{\alpha_0}c_0e^{-\lambda/\alpha_0}]\}^{-1}\) on the forward scaled exact-Pareto collision submodel

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.1 gives fixed heterogeneous-tail CTC endpoints; Theorem 4.3 gives fixed-fraction empirical-copula inference; Theorem 4.4 gives the gap-dependent intermediate-sequence CLT, proved in Appendix A.6.
Lemma 1 gives the fixed-common-index population CTC formula and Theorems 1--2 give its causal interpretation and empirical consistency.
Sections 2--3 define known-confounder-adjusted CTC and a generalized-Pareto parametric estimator, and Section 5 gives a permutation test for direct tail causality.

Definition 1 and Theorems 1--2 develop lagged maximum CTC for stationary Granger-type heavy-tailed VAR and nonlinear autoregressive time series, while Section 6 leaves its sampling distribution, bias correction, and rigorous testing open.
Theorems 2.1--2.2 establish univariate Pareto-tail LAN and its convolution lower bound.
Theorem 2.1 gives Gaussian approximation, asymptotic bias, and normality for smooth empirical tail-quantile functionals.

Theorem 3.2 is negative for the naive multiplier; Theorems 3.3--3.4 validate derivative and direct multipliers for one empirical tail-copula process under their conditions, not for the paired marked CTC statistic here.
Theorems 3.2 and 3.6 give adaptive scalar tail-coefficient intervals and an almost matching lower bound over separated second-order classes.
The paper gives an expected-length obstruction and worst-case-bias construction for uniformly valid scalar tail intervals.
The paper gives nonasymptotic minimax lower bounds for marginal heavy-tail parameters.

tldr: A local collision of innovation tail indices changes the finite-threshold CTC contrast on the logarithmic scale \(\Delta_n\log(n/k_n)\), while ordering information and second-order bias enter on the root-\(k_n\) scale. The model \(\Theta_{\mathrm{CTC}}(B)\) contains structural tuples and conditions honesty on a declared bias envelope, so orientation is never asserted to be a unique observational-law functional. The scaled exact-Pareto transition strictly refines the published fixed-index-order endpoints. The open program derives a growing marked-intensity experiment on the three feasible local faces, builds a finite-grid envelope-conditional three-valued direction set with a reported sensitivity family, and matches its tail-rank ambiguity probability by a contiguity lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Published CTC inference covers fixed common-index and fixed heterogeneous-index regimes, known-confounder-adjusted parametric estimation and permutation testing, and stationary lagged/max CTC. Proposition 3.1 and Theorems 4.3--4.4 of Leimenstoll and Schienle (2026), Pasche, Chavez-Demoulin, and Davison (2023), and Bodik, Paluš, and Pawlas (2024) do not treat a static independent triangular-array collision jointly with marked-mixture drift, second-order bias, or a minimax ambiguity loss.
project_justification.niche: The propagated-cause mixture depends on \(\Delta_n\log(n/k_n)\), whereas tail-order discrimination depends on \(\sqrt{k_n}\Delta_n\). Their exact relation \(h_n=\kappa_n\lambda_n\) produces three constrained local faces rather than an unconstrained two-coordinate LAN problem.
project_justification.fill: The scaled exact-Pareto curve anchors the object; the candidate normalized marked intensities and compensated central sequence make the experiment target explicit; the envelope-conditional confidence set and minimax criterion use the same structural class, local arrays, coverage class, information restriction, loss, and limit order.

related_work: Gnecco et al. (2021, Lemma 1 and Theorems 1--2) provide fixed-common-index comparable-tail CTC theory; they do not establish the unequal-index triangular-array balance condition used here, and Theorem 1 strictly enlarges their equality point to a local curve. Leimenstoll and Schienle (2026, Proposition 3.1) give fixed heterogeneous-tail endpoints, which Theorem 1 strictly refines locally. Their Theorem 4.1 is the independence and light-confounder CLT, Theorem 4.3 concerns fixed-fraction empirical-copula inference, and Theorem 4.4 is the gap-dependent intermediate-sequence heterogeneous-tail CLT with proof in Appendix A.6; these results inform, but do not supply, the joint collision experiment. Pasche, Chavez-Demoulin, and Davison (2023, Sections 2--3 and 5) remove much of a known confounder's effect, construct a generalized-Pareto parametric CTC estimator, and give a permutation test; their object is not an honest equality-boundary set and they do not study a static local index collision, its marked tail-rank experiment, or its minimax ambiguity loss. Bodik, Paluš, and Pawlas (2024, Definition 1, Theorems 1--2, Section 4, and Section 6) develop a lagged maximum CTC and estimator for stationary Granger-type heavy-tailed VAR and nonlinear autoregressive time series; they do not study differing-tail independent collisions, and explicitly leave distributional theory, bias correction, and rigorous testing open. Beirlant, Bouquiaux, and Werker (2006, Theorems 2.1--2.2) inform the root-\(k_n\) score and convolution argument. Drees (1998, Theorem 2.1) informs the second-order tail-process approximation. Bücher and Dette (2013, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) inform rank-process and multiplier calibration. Carpentier and Kim (2014, Theorems 3.2 and 3.6) and Sasaki and Wang (2024) inform scalar honest adaptation and declared worst-case bias control. Novak (2014) informs the heavy-tail testing lower-bound route.
technical_internal_limitation: The structural orientation is a component of \(\theta_n\), not an asserted functional of \(P_{\theta,n}\), and no unique structural representation is assumed. Every converse is restricted to \(\mathcal T_n\)-measurable procedures. It is not a lower bound for unrestricted causal discovery from the full distributional body, which may exploit non-tail non-Gaussian structure.
honest_scope: The scaled exact-Pareto local curve, structural witness membership, and scale geometry are theorem claims. Tangent existence, both conditional rank-mark kernels, the \(b_1,b_2\) drift, the information form, the uniform likelihood remainder, the envelope-conditional direction set, and the matching ambiguity frontier remain open-ended. Honesty is conditional on the declared envelope \(B_n\); the current assumptions do not identify or estimate that envelope, so the reported finite family \(B_n^{(c)}=cB_n\) is a sensitivity analysis rather than full adaptation to unknown bias. At \(\Delta_n=0\) and zero second-order bias, the experiment must reduce to the fixed-common-index CTC result; after projecting out marks, it must reduce to univariate tail-index LAN. The finite \(h\) face at \(\kappa=\infty\) has \(\lambda=0\); nonzero finite \(\lambda\) is a separated boundary with \( |h_n|\to\infty\), not part of that LAN compactum.
